item.title: The Once and Future Bathhouse - Public Books
item.description: Utilitarian public baths and pools once filled the world’s cities, but now new expensive spas are taking their place. Has even bathing become a luxury?

item.title: Extreme Circumstances, Extreme Reactions: Aaron Gwyn and Sean McCann - Public Books
item.description: “I come to the understanding I know nothing, and then I completely throw myself into the research.”

item.title: “Disaster Has Happened and Is Happening”: Tara Menon on What the Novel Reveals - Public Books
item.description: “I wanted to propose grief as perhaps the most appropriate response we can have to what is happening to the natural world—the disappearance of coral reefs in the Andaman Sea and bird habitats in New York.”

item.title: They Would Not Dream of Flowers: Translating Through the Tehran Blackout - Public Books
item.description: As the entire country was plunged into a digital blackout, the only light remaining in my room was the cold, clinical glow of my disconnected laptop. There, in that forced isolation, I sat translating a story about death.

item.title: Salsa For Salsa’s Sake - Public Books
item.description: When will we finally listen to a song for what it is, rather than for what it should have been?

item.title: B-Sides: Thomas De Quincey’s “The English Mail-Coach” - Public Books
item.description: “The English Mail-Coach” is one of the great meditations on mortality, on the speed with which life runs through our fingers, on how easily existence in all its radiance can be snuffed out.

item.title: The Waiting Is the Point: Time, Suffering, and Medicaid - Public Books
item.description: “To be poor and sick in America is to live in delay. The Medicaid system does not just reflect that reality—it enforces it.”

item.title: Álvaro Enrigue on “Now I Surrender” - Public Books
item.description: “Books just grow like trees. You cannot control them. They become something different than what you thought it was.”

item.title: Arendt Speaks of Oases - Public Books
item.description: Arendt sees the oasis as a way to save our self-understanding from the psychological cry of adjustment as well as the totalitarian demand for conformity.

item.title: Beautiful Sentences Matter: Billy-Ray Belcourt and Matt Hooley - Public Books
item.description: “Queer theory in general spoke to me in an embodied way, beyond its important theoretical work, because it revealed for me that beautiful sentences matter and that they can be critical aspects of the reading experience.”
